You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

[('arc_task_32be50b6_periodic_line_pattern_unresolved_test', 'ARC task-32be50b6 periodic line pattern (unresolved test)', 'Task 32be50b6 demonstrations showed a periodic-pattern completion task. For horizontal-row inputs, each nonzero full-width row is a stripe; outputs are horizontal stripe sequences tiled/repeated, including filling zero rows. Demonstrations: 9x9 row colors [0,0,9,6,1,9,4,9,4] -> [9,4,9,6,1,9,4,9,4]; 4x4 [0,0,9,4] -> [9,4,9,4]; 16x16 input stripe rows 2=5,4=3,5=8,6=7,7=6,15=5 -> output row-color sequence [7,6,5,5,3,8] repeated; 8x8 input [1,0,7,8,7,0,3,0] -> [1,3,7,8,7,1,3,7]. Diagonal examples likewise output full periodic color tilings from input diagonal traces. Important: the 28x28 test with rows 0=4, 7=9, 8=6, 11=1, 22=6, 23=3 remained unsolved after 8 attempts. Guesses using periods 6, 9, and 14, sparse/dense fills, and forward/backward holds were all wrong. Treat the test rule as unresolved; do not reuse guesses as verified. Demo requests were helpful.'), ('arc_stamp_motif_on_exact_zero_shape_matches', 'ARC: stamp motif on exact zero-shape matches', "For ARC grids with a sparse colored motif embedded in a noisy 0/background-color field, a task may ask to find every translation where the motif's colored-cell mask lands entirely on zeros, then recolor those zero cells with the motif color. Preserve the original motif and every nonmatching cell. Match the original orientation only; do not rotate or reflect unless demos show otherwise. Ignore motif bounding-box cells that are not colored: the match condition is that all motif cells land on 0, not that the whole bounding box matches a fixed pattern. Overlapping matches should produce the union of their motif cells. Demonstrated with a 3-colored 4x5 mask: two same-orientation placements on zeros were recolored, including overlaps, and output differences exactly equaled the union. Another 6-cell 1 mask in a 0/9 field had three placements; the output was the motif color at all their cells. Previous examples also confirmed no rotated/reflected matches. Use demos to verify target background, motif color, and whether orientation changes are allowed. Practical caution: transcribing a grid with even one omitted cell can hide a valid match and produce an invalid-sized output; verify every row has the stated width before matching and before submission. Confirmed again in task-58fa3f1c: a sparse 8-cell color-5 mask in a noisy 0/9 grid had exactly two translations whose mask cells were all 0; stamp 5 on both, preserve the original motif and all other cells.

Another accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c): on a 29x11 grid with background 6, scattered zero cells, and an 8-shaped L triomino with mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}, the rule was to stamp 8 over every translation whose three mask positions were all originally 0. There were 25 placements; preserve all 6s and unmatched 0s and take the union if placements overlap. This confirms the rule also applies when the nonzero background is 6 and the motif has only three colored cells. Compute matches from the original grid, not incrementally from already-stamped cells.

Additional accepted instance (task-58fa3f1c, 16x18): background 0 with scattered color-3 noise and a 7-cell color-2 stencil. In its 3x4 bounding box, the stencil mask offsets (0-indexed) are {(0,0),(0,2),(0,3),(1,1),(1,3),(2,1),(2,2)}. Search all in-bounds translations in the original input and accept one exactly when all seven mask cells are 0; bbox holes are irrelevant. There were 22 placements, with top-lefts (0,7),(0,9),(0,12),(1,3),(1,10),(1,11),(1,12),(3,1),(3,13),(4,2),(5,8),(7,5),(8,0),(8,1),(9,0),(9,1),(11,5),(12,6),(12,7),(12,8),(12,9),(13,6). Recolor the union of their mask cells to 2, preserving original stencil, color-3 noise, and unmatched zeros. Accepted first submission. Reinforces the same-orientation, original-grid mask match across another nonzero stencil color and a denser/asymmetric mask.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 13x13): background 8, zero target cells, and a 5-cell color-5 stencil with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1)} (a top horizontal bar with a two-cell stem below its center). Search original grid for translations whose five mask cells are all 0, ignoring other cells in the 3x3 bounding box. Four matching top-lefts were (2,1),(2,2),(2,4),(4,3). Recolor the union of those five-cell placements to 5; preserve all other cells and the original stencil. First submission accepted. This directly confirms the same-orientation mask-stamping rule for a 5-cell mask against zero speckles on background 8.

Accepted test (task-58fa3f1c, 28x13; background 9, motif color 8): The 9-cell mask offsets were {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(4,1),(5,0)}. Search only same-orientation translations where all mask positions are 0 in the original grid, ignoring bbox holes; recolor the union to 8. Valid top-lefts: (9,11) and (14,0). One failed submission contained a single accidental extra 8 at (15,11); ensure the row-5 endpoint of placement (9,11) is at row 14, not 15. The corrected output was accepted.


Newly verified 27x20 test (task-58fa3f1c): background 9, output/motif color 6; the source motif at rows 7-8, cols 16-19 has mask offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1,3)}. Valid same-orientation translations whose four mask cells are all original 0s have top-lefts (2,14),(3,15),(5,1),(6,10),(7,7),(11,15),(14,13),(15,4),(15,5),(15,6),(16,1),(18,13),(21,3),(21,11),(25,5). Recolor the 55-cell union to 6. The first submission used the correct rule but failed because input was mis-transcribed at (16,19): the true value is 9, not 0. Corrected output was accepted. Check source input values against the prompt, not only row widths; one bad copied digit can make an unchanged cell wrong even if it does not affect the match set. Five fresh demonstrations with varying sparse stencil masks/background colors further confirmed the same rule: same-orientation translations only, match on mask cells being 0, ignore bbox holes, take union of overlaps, and preserve the source stencil and all other cells."), ('arc_task_c3e8f639_decode_3x3_cells_by_ignoring_color_5', 'ARC task-c3e8f639: decode 3x3 cells by ignoring color 5', 'For ARC task-c3e8f639, the input is a grid tiled into 3x3 cells. Produce an output grid with one cell per 3x3 input block. In each block, ignore color 5, which is the background, and output the single remaining color present (including 0 as a valid output color). The demo was 24x24 -> 8x8 and the test was 21x21 -> 7x7; every macro-cell contained only one non-5 color, so this is a direct 3x3-to-1x1 compression. Example test output was [[0,3,0,0,0,0,0],[0,0,3,2,0,0,0],[2,0,0,9,0,0,2],[9,3,0,2,0,0,0],[0,2,9,0,0,9,0],[2,3,2,0,0,9,0],[0,0,0,0,2,0,9]].

Additional accepted test (6x6 -> 2x2): split from top-left into four aligned 3x3 tiles; ignore 5 and emit the sole other color, with 0 retained as a valid result. Test input tiles decoded to [[0,1],[0,0]]; the 1 occurred once in the upper-right tile, and all other tiles contained only 0 and 5. Correct on first submission with no demos. This confirms very small 6x6 cases use the same exact 3x3 compression.'), ('arc_task_7a6f1448_complete_line_recoloring_demos_test_contradiction', 'ARC task-7a6f1448: recolor complete uniform rows and columns to 2', "Task task-7a6f1448 rule: identify every full row and every full column whose cells are all the same input color (examples have noisy two-color grids and different line colors), recolor exactly the cells in those complete lines to 2, and leave every other cell unchanged. Six demonstrations confirmed this for line colors 0, 3, 4, 6, and 9 across varied grid sizes. Fresh 15x7 test with colors 8 and 3 had complete 8-lines at rows 2 and 14 and column 0 (0-based); converting exactly those lines to 2 solved it. Important validation: I first submitted this rule incorrectly because I accidentally changed two additional adjacent 8s at (row 7, col 1) and (row 11, col 1), which are NOT part of any complete line. The corrected output left them 8 and was accepted. Construct output with an explicit mask (full uniform rows/cols), then verify all non-mask cells are unchanged. Earlier note about a contradictory test and failed guesses may reflect accidental extra modifications; do not infer a hidden condition from it without rechecking exact output coordinates.

Additional accepted test (26x23): two-color input uses 5/9. The only full uniform rows were row indices 9 and 25, each all 9; the only full uniform columns were column indices 9, 15, 18, and 22, each all 9 (0-based). Recolor the union of those complete lines to 2; leave all other cells unchanged. This output was accepted with zero wrong attempts. Construct with an explicit mask; intersections are recolored once and no neighboring partial-line cells should change.

Additional accepted test (9x26): input colors 9/6. Recolor complete uniform rows 2 and 8 and complete uniform columns 3, 9, 13, 16, 21, and 25 (0-based) to 2. Preserve isolated 6s at (3,18), (5,4), and (6,11), since they are not in complete uniform lines. Output accepted with zero wrong attempts.

Additional accepted test (14x13): the input had a complete uniform color-3 row at index 8 and complete uniform color-3 column at index 8 (0-based). Recolor the union of row 8 and column 8 to color 2; preserve all other cells, including non-complete partial 3s. Accepted with zero wrong attempts. This further confirms the rule is to find complete same-color rows/columns, independent of marker color, and recolor only their cells.

Additional accepted test (5x22): input is color 4 with color-3 cells, and the complete uniform color-3 lines are row 4 and columns 6 and 15 (0-based). Recolor the union of those lines to color 2; preserve every other cell, including partial color-3 columns. The resulting 5x22 output was accepted. The same JSON grid was initially reported as an invalid ARC grid, then accepted on immediate resubmission, so that first rejection appears transient rather than evidence against the rule.

Additional accepted test (14x13): input colors were 8 and 6. Complete uniform color-6 rows were indices 2, 9, and 12; complete uniform color-6 columns were indices 1 and 7 (0-based). Recolor the union of these lines to 2, preserving all other cells; accepted with zero wrong attempts. This confirms the line mask applies even where the line's input color equals other noisy cells, and row/column intersections simply belong to the union.

Additional accepted test (14x13): input colors were 8 and 6. Complete uniform color-6 rows were indices 2, 9, and 12; complete uniform color-6 columns were indices 1 and 7 (0-based). Recolor the union of these lines to 2, preserving all other cells; accepted with zero wrong attempts. This confirms the line mask applies even where the line's input color equals other noisy cells, and row/column intersections simply belong to the union."), ('arc_task_2fd86235_decode_uniform_corner_cells_in_stripe_grid', 'ARC task-2fd86235: decode uniform-corner cells in stripe grid', "For ARC task-2fd86235, the input is a regular lattice/grid of large uniform-color cells whose divider lines are mostly one color. Some divider intersections are recolored with marker colors. Find the bounding box of all non-background marker junctions on the lattice. The output has one cell per lattice rectangle between consecutive junction rows/columns inside that marker bbox. Set an output cell to marker color X only when all four corner junctions of that rectangle are X; otherwise use the large interior fill color. Ignore rectangles outside the marker bounding box. This is confirmed by demos: e.g. a 1 color 2x2 set of junctions produces one 1 output cell, while incomplete/mixed corner rectangles remain fill color; marker runs can create adjoining same-color output cells when all four corners match. For the test instance, nodes rows 3,6,9,12,15,18 and cols 2,8,14,20,26 yielded 5x4 output [[7,7,0,0],[5,7,7,7],[5,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9]]. Key pitfall: do NOT color an output cell merely because top/one edge endpoints match; require all four corners. Determine crop as min/max marker junction bbox, output dimensions are intervals between those lattice lines.

Accepted test instance (24x28): lattice junction lines at rows 0,5,10,15,20 and columns 0,6,12,18,24; separator color 3, broad cell fill 2. Junction colors by row were [3,3,3,7,7], [6,6,3,7,7], [6,6,3,3,3], [3,1,1,8,8], [3,1,1,8,8]. Applying the all-four-corners-same-marker rule within the marker junction bbox gives accepted 4x4 output [[2,2,2,7],[6,2,2,2],[2,2,2,2],[2,1,2,8]].

Additional accepted test (20x26): horizontal junction rows 0, 8, 16 and the marker-bbox columns 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 produce node matrix [[5,5,2,2,3,3],[5,5,5,5,3,3],[2,2,5,5,2,2]]. The broad interior fill is 9. Requiring all four corners of each cell to match yields accepted output [[5,9,9,9,3],[9,9,5,9,9]]. Important transcription pitfall: row 8 has color 5 at columns 8, 11, 14, and 17. The first output cell is 5 because all four corners at rows 0/8 and columns 8/11 are 5. A first submission that mistakenly read row 8 column 11 as 2 was rejected; correcting the node-color extraction fixed it. A separate demo confirms unmatched/mixed corner cells use the broad interior fill (e.g. 7), while a same-color four-corner cell is copied to output.


Accepted test (30x26; task instance solved with 0 wrong submissions): background/interior fill 1, separator lattice color 3, junction marker 9. Horizontal lattice rows were 4, 12, 20, 28; vertical lattice columns were 1, 8, 15, 22. Within the marker-junction bounding box rows 4..20 and columns 1..22, the node-color matrix is [[9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9],[3,9,9,3]]. Use the adjacent intervals only: row intervals 4-12 and 12-20, column intervals 1-8, 8-15, 15-22. The first output row has all four corners equal to 9 in each rectangle; the second row's left and right rectangles have mixed 3/9 corners, while the middle rectangle has all corners 9. Accepted output: [[9,9,9],[1,9,1]]. The outer row 28 is beyond the maximal marker row and is excluded; the full non-marker separator intersections (color 3) are not treated as marker colors.

Additional accepted test (30x30): broad fill 5, separator lattice color 7. Junction rows 0 and 27, junction columns 4 and 24; all four intersections are marker color 4. The marker-junction bbox contains exactly these 2x2 nodes, so there is one rectangle and all corners match: accepted output [[4]]. Do not emit a 30x30 image or preserve the large grid spacing; output is the coarse cell matrix.

Additional accepted test (24x28): broad cell fill 1, separator color 9; horizontal lattice rows 1,4,7,10,13,16,19,22 and vertical lattice columns 3,7,11,15,19,23,27. Non-9 marker junction bbox spans rows 7..22 and columns 3..27, so use the six junction rows [7,10,13,16,19,22] and seven junction columns [3,7,11,15,19,23,27] to form a 5x6 output. The node-color matrix is [[9,9,9,4,4,3,3],[5,5,4,4,4,3,3],[5,5,4,4,8,8,9],[5,5,9,9,8,8,8],[4,4,7,7,8,8,8],[4,4,7,7,8,8,9]]. As usual, output marker color only when all four corners match; otherwise fill 1. Accepted output: [[1,1,1,4,1,3],[5,1,4,1,1,1],[5,1,1,1,8,1],[1,1,1,1,8,8],[4,1,7,1,8,1]]. Note separator-colored nodes (9) can bound the bbox/runs but a cell with all four 9 corners is not a marker result; the output fill is used for mixed or separator-only corners.


Additional accepted test (14x28; zero wrong submissions): separator color 5, broad cell fill 8. Horizontal junction rows are 0, 4, 8, 12 and vertical junction columns 0, 8, 16, 24. Junction colors are [[1,1,4,4],[1,1,4,4],[5,5,4,4],[5,5,5,5]]. The non-separator marker bbox spans rows 0..8 and columns 0..24, so use node rows [0,4,8] and columns [0,8,16,24], forming a 2x3 output. Apply the all-four-corners-same-color rule excluding separator color 5; all other cells use fill 8. Accepted output: [[1,8,4],[8,8,4]]. In particular, nodes colored 5 inside the marker bbox are retained when computing mixed-corner cells; omit the outer row 12 because it is beyond the marker bbox."), ('arc_task_c3e8f639_decode_3x3_noisy_color_tiles', 'ARC task-c3e8f639: decode 3x3 noisy-color tiles', 'For ARC task-c3e8f639, the input is a large grid partitioned into 3x3 tiles. Each tile encodes one output cell by filling most non-background pixels with its symbol color amid noise/background color 5. For the 30x30 test, each 3x3 tile contained 0s, 5s, and 8s; output was 10x10, where each cell is the more frequent of 0 and 8 within its corresponding 3x3 block (ignore 5). Demo confirmed the reduction: 21x21 input became 7x7 output by decoding each 3x3 block, choosing the non-5 symbol color. In the test, no 0/8 ties occurred. General procedure: partition from top-left into 3x3 blocks and output the most frequent non-background color in each.'), ('arc_task_175542bf_four_rotated_copies_in_2x2_tiling', 'ARC task-175542bf: four rotated copies in 2x2 tiling', 'For task-175542bf, enlarge an H×W input to 2H×2W by placing four orientations in quadrants: top-left = original; top-right = 90° clockwise rotation; bottom-left = 90° counterclockwise rotation; bottom-right = 180° rotation. All quadrants retain the original colors. Demo 6×6→12×12 confirms rotations: for example top-right first row is original first column bottom-to-top; bottom-left first row is original last column top-to-bottom; bottom-right first row is original last row reversed. Solved 4×4 test with three color-3 cells.

Additional accepted test (14×14 -> 28×28): input contained colors 4 and 8; output was formed exactly by concatenating the original at top-left, 90° clockwise rotation at top-right, 90° counterclockwise rotation at bottom-left, and 180° rotation at bottom-right. Accepted on first submission. This confirms the same rule on a larger 14×14 input and that no recoloring or other transformation is needed.
